subject: Web Systems
title: Node.js Foundations + Docker Intro — Prelim Reviewer Quiz (60 Items)

questions.text: Which keyword declares a block-scoped variable that cannot be reassigned?
questions.hint: Object/array contents can still change, but the binding itself cannot be reassigned.

questions.text: What does typeof null return in JavaScript?
questions.hint: This is a well-known historical quirk in JavaScript.

questions.text: What is the result of Boolean([])?
questions.hint: Empty arrays are truthy in JavaScript.

questions.text: Which array method returns a new array after transforming each item?
questions.hint: It creates a new array of the same length with transformed values.

questions.text: What does the === operator compare?
questions.hint: Always prefer === over == to avoid unexpected type coercion.

questions.text: What is a closure in JavaScript?
options: A function that remembers variables from its outer scope even after that scope has finished
A method to close file streams
questions.hint: Closures enable private state and are the foundation of many patterns.

questions.text: Which of the following is a falsy value?
questions.hint: Falsy values: false, 0, "", null, undefined, NaN.

questions.text: What is the primary role of the V8 engine in Node.js?
questions.hint: V8 is Google's JS engine, also used in Chrome.

questions.text: Why can Node.js handle many concurrent connections without spawning a thread per request?
options: It uses multiple CPU cores by default
It is single-threaded and non-blocking via the event loop
It uses worker threads for every request
questions.hint: I/O is handed off; callbacks run when ready.

questions.text: Which of the following is a core Node.js module that requires no installation?
questions.hint: Core modules include fs, path, http, events, etc.

questions.text: What does process.argv[0] typically contain?
options: The first argument passed by the user
The path to the script being executed
The path to the Node.js executable
questions.hint: argv[1] is usually the script path; argv[2+] are user arguments.

questions.text: Which module is used to build cross-platform-safe file paths?
questions.hint: path.join() correctly handles / vs \ depending on the OS.

questions.text: Which is the correct way to read a file with async/await using the promises API?
questions.hint: You must await the Promise returned by fs.promises.readFile.

questions.text: What does path.basename("/home/user/index.js") return?
questions.hint: basename returns the last portion of the path.

questions.text: Why should you use path.join() instead of hardcoding slashes?
options: It is faster than string concatenation
It builds the correct path separator for the current OS
It checks whether the path exists
questions.hint: Hardcoded / breaks on Windows; path.join handles it correctly.

questions.text: Which semver range allows minor and patch updates but not major version changes?
questions.hint: ^ means compatible with version (minor/patch OK).

questions.text: What is the difference between dependencies and devDependencies?
options: dependencies are needed at runtime; devDependencies are only for development
questions.hint: Production installs skip devDependencies by default.

questions.text: Which is considered the cleanest asynchronous pattern, built on top of Promises?
questions.hint: async/await makes asynchronous code look synchronous and is easier to reason about.

questions.text: When do microtasks (Promises and process.nextTick) run in the Node.js event loop?
options: Between each phase, before the next phase starts
questions.hint: Microtasks have higher priority and run before the next event-loop phase.

questions.text: Which of the following runs first?
options: They all run at the same time
questions.hint: process.nextTick has the highest priority among these.

questions.text: What is the conventional exit code for success in Node.js?
questions.hint: 0 = success; any non-zero value signals failure.

questions.text: What is an operational error?
options: A bug in the programmer's code
An expected failure such as a missing file or bad user input
A crash of the V8 engine
An error that always kills the process
questions.hint: Operational errors should be handled gracefully; programmer errors should crash loudly in development.

questions.text: What is the recommended view of process.on("uncaughtException")?
options: It should be the primary error-handling strategy
It is a safety net, not a substitute for proper try/catch
It is required in every Node application
It is the only way to catch asynchronous errors
questions.hint: Never rely on it as the main way to handle errors.

questions.text: Why should secrets (API keys, passwords) never be hardcoded in source code?
options: They can be committed to version control and accidentally exposed
Hardcoded values are slower at runtime
questions.hint: Use environment variables (and .env files) instead.

questions.text: Which HTTP status code means the client is authenticated but not permitted to access the resource?
questions.hint: 401 = not authenticated; 403 = authenticated but forbidden.

questions.text: Which status code indicates the request format is valid but fails validation rules?
questions.hint: 422 Unprocessable Entity is commonly used for validation failures.

questions.text: What is an EventEmitter?
options: An object that emits named events and allows listeners to register for them
A stream that emits data chunks
questions.hint: http.Server itself is an EventEmitter.

questions.text: What problem do Streams solve compared to fs.readFile?
options: They process data in chunks so memory usage stays flat
questions.hint: Large files never need to be fully loaded into memory.

questions.text: Which stream type reads data, transforms it, and then writes the result?
questions.hint: Transform streams are a special kind of Duplex.

questions.text: What does the .pipe() method do in Node.js streams?
options: Connects the output of a readable stream to a writable stream
questions.hint: Example: fs.createReadStream(...).pipe(fs.createWriteStream(...))

questions.text: Which HTTP method is idempotent and typically used to retrieve data?
questions.hint: Calling GET multiple times should have the same effect as calling it once.

questions.text: Where is data typically sent in a POST request?
questions.hint: GET data is in the URL; POST data is in the body.

questions.text: Which status code is commonly returned after a successful POST that creates a new resource?
questions.hint: 201 Created indicates a new resource was successfully created.

questions.text: What is the difference between a Docker image and a container?
options: An image is a running instance; a container is the blueprint
An image is a read-only blueprint; a container is a running instance of that image
A container is larger than an image
questions.hint: Image = recipe; container = the running dish.

questions.text: How does a container differ from a virtual machine?
options: Containers virtualize an entire operating system
Containers share the host kernel and isolate only the process (lightweight)
questions.hint: Containers are much lighter and faster to start than VMs.

questions.text: Why should you copy package*.json and run npm install before copying the rest of the source code in a Dockerfile?
options: It takes advantage of Docker layer caching so dependencies are not reinstalled on every code change
npm install must run first or the build fails
It is required by the Node base image
questions.hint: If only source code changes, the npm install layer can be reused.

questions.text: What does the -p 3000:3000 flag mean in docker run?
options: It sets the container's internal port to 3000
It maps host port 3000 to container port 3000
It limits the container to 3000 MB of memory
questions.hint: Format is hostPort:containerPort.

questions.text: Why should node_modules be listed in .dockerignore?
options: It makes the image build fail otherwise
The local node_modules may be for a different OS/architecture; npm install should run inside the container
Docker cannot copy the node_modules folder
It is required by the official Node image
questions.hint: Always install dependencies inside the container for consistency.

questions.text: Which Dockerfile instruction sets the working directory inside the container?
questions.hint: WORKDIR /app is a common pattern.

questions.text: Which command builds a Docker image from a Dockerfile in the current directory and tags it?
questions.hint: docker build -t <name> .

questions.text: Which status code means "Success, but there is nothing to send back" (common for DELETE)?
questions.hint: 204 No Content.

questions.text: Which status code indicates a client error caused by a malformed request?
questions.hint: 400 Bad Request.

questions.text: Where must the await keyword be used?
questions.hint: await is only legal inside functions marked async.

questions.text: Which method returns the file extension of a path?
questions.hint: path.extname("file.txt") → ".txt"

questions.text: What is the recommended way to create a custom error type?
questions.hint: class ValidationError extends Error { ... }

questions.text: Which semver range allows only patch-level updates?
questions.hint: ~1.2.3 allows 1.2.x but not 1.3.0.

questions.text: Which stream type can both be read from and written to?
questions.hint: Duplex supports both directions; Transform is a special Duplex.

questions.text: In a raw http.createServer callback, which properties tell you the requested method and path?
questions.hint: You branch logic with if (req.method === "GET" && req.url === "/...")

questions.text: Which Dockerfile instruction documents the port the application listens on?
questions.hint: EXPOSE 3000 is documentation; -p still needed at runtime.

questions.text: What is the purpose of a .dockerignore file?
options: It lists packages that should not be installed
It excludes files and folders from being copied into the Docker image
It prevents the container from starting
It is required for multi-stage builds
questions.hint: Similar idea to .gitignore — keep node_modules, .git, .env out of the image.
This is a classic closure / function-factory example.
Look at the object passed to JSON.stringify.

questions.text: The Node.js global object that provides access to CLI arguments, environment variables, and process exit.
questions.hint: process.argv, process.env, process.exit()

questions.text: The package.json field used for packages needed only during development (not in production).
questions.hint: Opposite of the "dependencies" field.

questions.text: The pattern where a function remembers the variables from the scope in which it was created, even after that outer function has finished running.
questions.hint: Also called a lexical closure.

questions.text: The type of error that represents a bug in the code (as opposed to expected bad input or missing files).
questions.hint: Also accept "programming error" or "bug".

questions.text: The semver prefix that allows only patch-level updates (e.g., 1.2.3 → 1.2.x but not 1.3.0).
questions.hint: Tilde (~) vs caret (^).

questions.text: The core Node.js module that provides the EventEmitter class.
questions.hint: const { EventEmitter } = require("events");

questions.text: The HTTP status code that means the client is authenticated but is not allowed to access the requested resource.
questions.hint: Forbidden (distinct from 401 Unauthorized).
